DO NOT USE SANI-CLOTH PLUS WIPES OR ANY OTHER CLEANERS THAT WILL RUIN ACRYLIC TO CLEAN OUT CHAMBERS!!!!! Only use a mild bleach solution or Clorox Wipes to clean out the chambers. If you have questions about what to use, contact someone before cleaning.
Wipe/rinse out the chamber thoroughly, including plastic mesh grates at bottom of chambers.

Remove water bottles from lids ♦ Loosen the nut where the water bottle is fastened to the lid and pull the water bottle up. ♦ Empty water bottles and wash out. steps.title: Perform Initial Body Composition
steps.instruction: Take body composition measurements via QMR before placing animals into the experiment.

steps.title: Set Up Cages and Food Intake Chambers
steps.instruction: Prepare the cages and supply food and water to the animals.

substeps.instruction: Weigh animals and place them into Food Intake chambers.
Fill food hoppers: turn the feeding tube upside down (metal mesh at bottom) and fill 90% full with diet.
Slide a metal washer onto the center post of the feed tube.
Using the red handled tool, slide the larger catch bin onto the tool, followed by the spring.
Position the tool over the center post and slide the spring and catch bin over the feeding tube.
Align slot holes in the catch bin with the slots in the feeding tubes; push down and twist to lock snugly.
Place the full feeding tube on top of each scale and place the chamber over the top.
Ensure chamber lids are clasped firmly and evenly.

steps.title: Maintain Drierite and Soda Lime
steps.instruction: Inspect and replace Drierite (if pink) and Soda Lime (if not white).

substeps.instruction: Remove canister from holder and unscrew the lid (hoses can remain attached).
Remove spring, metal lid, and cotton filter.
Empty old material and replace with new, ensuring not to fill past the top hole in the canister.
Tap the bottom of the canister to tamp down the material.
Reinsert components in this order: cotton filter, metal disc, spring, then screw on the top.
Push the canister back onto the holder.

steps.title: Initialize System Power and Software
steps.instruction: Power on the hardware and initialize the Oxymax software.

substeps.instruction: Turn on all surge protectors and verify power lights are on; power on and log into the PC.
Run 'Oxymax for Windows' and select the appropriate hardware configuration.
Allow the system to perform a scan; if error messages occur, check hardware and select 'Refresh'.
Allow approximately 2 hours of warm-up time before calibration or starting the experiment.

steps.title: Prepare Gas Sensor Calibration
steps.instruction: Configure the system for calibration using Primary Standard Grade gas (20.50% Oxygen, 0.50% Carbon Dioxide, balanced with Nitrogen).

substeps.instruction: Navigate to calibration via 'Tools >> Calibration' (before experiment) or 'Experiment >> Calibration' (after experiment).
Verify actual gas concentrations are registered for 'Span' gases (Zero gases should be 0).
Click 'Cal Gas' next to the sensor group label, make changes, select 'Apply', then 'Close'.
Set the sample flow meter on the System Sample Pump to approximately 400 mL/min (indicator ball on top of the .4 L/min line).
Set the outlet pressure on the calibration gas tank regulator to between 5-10 PSI.
Insert the calibration gas tank tube into the open T-fitting end of the calibration sample tube on the back of the sample pump; verify gas flow from the exhaust tube.

steps.title: Calibrate Oxygen (O2) Sensor
steps.instruction: Perform the O2 sensor calibration procedure.

substeps.instruction: Click the 'Calibrate' button under the 'O2' header.
Verify sample flow is ~400 mL/min and cal gas pressure is 5-10 psi with exhaust flow.
Click 'NEXT' to purge the sensor with cal gas.

When the target O2 concentration is displayed, use the 'Course Gain' and 'Fine Gain' knobs to adjust the displayed concentration until it matches the target (values will turn green). Wait a few minutes for lag time.
Click 'Next' and then 'Finish'. Immediately proceed to CO2 calibration.

steps.title: Calibrate Carbon Dioxide (CO2) Sensor
steps.instruction: Perform the CO2 sensor calibration procedure.

substeps.instruction: Click the 'Calibrate' button under the 'CO2' header.
Ensure cal gas is on and the Soda Lime column is WHITE (replace if not white, as it is used for 'CO2 Zero' calibration).
Click 'NEXT' to purge the sensor; the system will measure the 'Zero' point.
The system will then purge the 'Span' gas and measure the necessary gain.
Review the calculated offset and gain displayed by Oxymax.
Turn off the cal gas flow and click 'Finish'.
Note: Do not recalibrate between fed and fasting cycles.

steps.title: Analyze Data using CLAX
steps.instruction: Use the CLAX program to manage and export experimental data.

substeps.instruction: Open the CLAX program and select 'Add Experiment' on the 'Manage Databench' screen to open the desired file.
Use the 'Experiments' tab to view hardware/experiment configurations and set light/dark cycle times.
Use the 'Subjects' tab to view body weights and add/assign tags (e.g., genotype, gender) to animal IDs.
Use the 'Measurements' tab to create equations for measurements.
Select the 'Data' icon to view raw data, including High Resolution feeding data (consumption at selected intervals) and Feeding Bouts data (duration and consumption of each meal).
Export data to other programs (Excel, Prism) using 'Export and Copy to Clipboard'.
Utilize Statistics, Time Graphs, Box Plot, Histogram, and Correlation tools for visualization.
